original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: For which of the 216 diagonal three-register targets in the paid S3 alphabet of open PR #3893 does the two-dimensional representation rank equal the direct generator bill, and what is the largest sharp floor?
scope_change_reason: The drawn card was r437-carrier-integration. Its compiler, caller and reverse-coefficient stock obligations are already open in #4176 and #4183, and #4147 already derived the coefficient 1123650. This package takes the next suggestion and the screening question left by open #3893: the same S3 alphabet, every diagonal target, without a new construction round.
bottleneck_link: A sharp floor above the published four-call target would be a stronger obstruction inside this nonabelian alphabet. A gap between generator length and represented rank shows where that obstruction is not yet sharp.
stop_rule: Stop after classifying all 216 diagonal targets and checking the coordinate words that meet the rank bound. Do not search shared words for the gapped transposition.
evidence: Every label except the transposition (13) has generator length equal to rank(rho(g)+I). Exactly 125 of 216 triples match, and the coordinate concatenation attains the bound for each of them. Eight triples, all labels in the two length-two elements, have sharp floor 6. The transposition (13) has length 3 and represented rank 1, so the other 91 triples are not sharp by this comparison.
author: Riquelme Soares (@hevlyo)
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance was used for the classification, the group-algebra check and the write-up. No independent human review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Can a shared word shorter than length 3 write the transposition (13) on one register in this same paid alphabet?
open_questions.why_it_matters: That element is the only label whose generator length exceeds its represented rank. A shorter word would lower the direct bill of every triple that contains it.
open_questions.first_step: Search words in the two paid labels whose product is (13), allowing more than one register of scratch, and stop at the first word shorter than 3 or at an exhaustive length-2 miss.
open_questions.blocked_by: A one-register word cannot be shorter than 3, and no legal scratch register is specified by the #3893 alphabet.
